1.1/O1.name: Commutative
1.1/O1.note: The order of two terms or two factors may be swapped.

1.1/O1.name: Associative
1.1/O1.note: The grouping may be changed; the order may not.

1.1/O1.name: Distributive
1.1/O1.note: Since $b-c$ means $b+(-c)$, the subtraction form is the same statement. Read right to left, it takes out a common factor.

1.1/O2.name: Substitution
1.1/O2.statement: Replace each variable with its value, then evaluate.

1.1/O2.name: Negatives go in parentheses
1.1/O2.note: Substituting without parentheses gives $-3^{2}=-9$, a different number.

1.1/O3.name: Order of operations
1.1/O3.statement: Parentheses, then exponents, then $\times$ and $\div$ left to right, then $+$ and $-$ left to right.

1.1/O3.name: What counts as grouping
1.1/O3.statement: Parentheses, the fraction bar, and the radical all group.
1.1/O3.note: Everything above a fraction bar is divided by everything below it.

1.1/O3.name: Exponents and the minus sign
1.1/O3.note: The exponent applies to 9 unless parentheses place the minus inside the base. The same distinction makes $b^{2}-4ac$ come out right in the quadratic formula in 1.7.

1.1/O4.name: Order on the number line
1.1/O4.statement: $a<b$ means $a$ lies to the left of $b$.

1.1/O4.name: Comparing across forms
1.1/O4.statement: Write both numbers in one form first: $\tfrac{3}{8}=0.375$, so $\tfrac{3}{8}<0.4$.

1.1/O5.name: Interval notation
1.1/O5.statement: $(a,b)$ excludes both ends, $[a,b]$ includes both, $[a,b)$ includes only the left.

1.1/O5.name: On the graph
1.1/O5.statement: A hollow dot excludes the endpoint, a solid dot includes it.

1.2/O1.name: Base and exponent
1.2/O1.statement: $a^{n}$ is $a$ used as a factor $n$ times. $a$ is the base, $n$ the exponent.

1.2/O1.name: Where the minus sits
1.2/O1.note: In the second, only the 2 is raised.

1.2/O1.name: Sign of a power of a negative
1.2/O1.statement: An even power is positive, an odd power is negative.

1.2/O2.name: Power rule
1.2/O2.note: A power of a power multiplies.

1.2/O3.name: Polynomial vocabulary
1.2/O3.statement: term, coefficient, degree of a term, degree of the polynomial, leading coefficient

1.2/O3.name: Degree
1.2/O3.statement: The degree of a polynomial is the highest degree among its terms.

1.2/O3.name: Leading coefficient
1.2/O3.statement: In $-4x^{3}+7x^{2}-x+9$ the degree is 3 and the leading coefficient is $-4$.
1.2/O3.note: The sign belongs to the coefficient.

1.2/O3.name: By number of terms
1.2/O3.statement: one term monomial, two binomial, three trinomial

1.2/O4.name: Like terms
1.2/O4.statement: Same variable raised to the same exponent: $5x^{2}$ and $2x^{2}$ are like, $5x^{2}$ and $3x$ are not.

1.2/O4.name: Adding
1.2/O4.statement: Add the coefficients of like terms; the exponent does not change.

1.2/O5.name: Distribute term by term
1.2/O5.statement: Every term of the first factor multiplies every term of the second.

1.2/O6.name: Building the polynomial
1.2/O6.statement: Turn the described quantity into an expression, then evaluate it at the stated value.

1.3/O1.name: What the GCF is
1.3/O1.statement: The greatest common factor of the coefficients, times the lowest power of each variable common to every term.

1.3/O1.name: Worked example
1.3/O1.note: $6$ divides 12 and 18; $x^{2}$ is the lowest power present.

1.3/O1.name: Check by expanding
1.3/O1.statement: Multiply the factored form out; it must equal the original polynomial.

1.3/O1.name: Completely
1.3/O1.statement: Nothing common may remain inside the bracket.
1.3/O1.note: $6x(2x^{2}-3x)$ is a true factorisation but not complete: $x$ still divides both terms inside.

1.3/O2.name: Factoring $x^{2}+bx+c$
1.3/O2.note: For $x^{2}+7x+12$, $2\cdot 6=12$ but $2+6\ne 7$, so $2$ and $6$ do not work.

1.3/O2.name: Reading the signs
1.3/O2.statement: $c>0$: $p$ and $q$ share the sign of $b$.  $c<0$: they have opposite signs.

1.3/O3.name: Product and sum
1.3/O3.statement: Find two numbers with product $ac$ and sum $b$.

1.3/O3.name: Always check
1.3/O3.note: $3$ and $1$ placed as $(2x+3)(x+1)$ give $5x$; placed as $(2x+1)(x+3)$ they give $7x$.

1.4/O1.name: Factor first
1.4/O1.statement: Factor the numerator and the denominator completely, then cancel.

1.4/O1.name: Only factors cancel
1.4/O1.note: The bar groups the whole numerator; a 3 cannot be cancelled against one term of it.

1.4/O1.name: Restrictions
1.4/O1.statement: The denominator may never be zero; exclude the values that make it so.

1.4/O2.name: Multiplying
1.4/O2.statement: Factor everything, cancel across the fraction bar, then multiply what is left.

1.5/O1.name: Negative exponent
1.5/O1.note: A negative exponent means a reciprocal, not a negative answer: $2^{-3}=\tfrac{1}{8}$.

1.5/O1.name: The rules still hold
1.5/O1.statement: Product, quotient and power rules work for negative integers too.

1.6/O1.name: Addition property
1.6/O1.statement: Adding the same quantity to both sides keeps the equation true.

1.6/O1.name: Multiplication property
1.6/O1.statement: Multiplying both sides by the same non-zero quantity keeps it true.

1.6/O1.name: Solving for the variable
1.6/O1.statement: Collect the variable on one side and the numbers on the other, then divide by the coefficient.

1.6/O1.name: Check
1.6/O1.statement: Substitute the answer back into the original equation.

1.6/O2.name: Clear the fractions
1.6/O2.statement: Multiply both sides by the LCD of every denominator.
1.6/O2.note: Every term, including the ones that are not fractions.

1.6/O3.name: Solving for one letter among several
1.6/O3.statement: Treat the other letters as if they were numbers.

1.6/O3.name: When the target appears twice
1.6/O3.statement: Collect its terms on one side and factor it out, then divide by the bracket.

1.6/O4.name: Translating a word problem
1.6/O4.statement: Name the unknown, write the equation the words describe, solve it, then read the answer back against the question.

1.7/O1.name: Standard form first
1.7/O1.statement: $ax^{2}+bx+c=0$: everything on one side, zero on the other.

1.7/O1.name: Zero-product property
1.7/O1.note: $AB=6$ gives no such conclusion: the product must be $0$.

1.7/O1.name: Worked example
1.7/O1.note: The roots are the opposites of the numbers in the brackets.

1.7/O2.name: Reading a, b, c
1.7/O2.note: The signs belong to the coefficients.

1.7/O2.name: Discriminant
1.7/O2.statement: $b^{2}-4ac$ positive gives two real solutions, zero gives one, negative gives none.
The formula solves any quadratic, including those that do not factor.
1.7/O2.name: Applies to every quadratic

1.1/O6.name: Definition of absolute value
1.1/O6.statement: $|a|$ is the distance from $a$ to 0 on the number line.

1.1/O6.name: The bars group
1.1/O6.note: Evaluate inside first. $|3|-|7|=-4$ is a different calculation and a different answer.

1.1/O6.name: Where the minus sits
1.1/O6.note: The bars apply only to what is inside them: $|-5|=5$, and the outside minus then gives $-5$.

2.1/O1.name: Ordered pair
2.1/O1.statement: $(x,y)$: the first number is the horizontal position, the second the vertical.

2.1/O1.name: Quadrants
2.1/O1.statement: Numbered I to IV anticlockwise from the upper right: I is $(+,+)$, II is $(-,+)$, III is $(-,-)$, IV is $(+,-)$.

2.1/O1.name: On an axis
2.1/O1.statement: A point with a $0$ coordinate lies on an axis and is in no quadrant.
2.1/O1.note: $(0,1)$ is on the $y$-axis; $(4,0)$ is on the $x$-axis.

2.1/O2.name: Checking a pair
2.1/O2.statement: Substitute the first number for $x$ and the second for $y$; the pair is a solution when the two sides agree.

2.1/O3.name: Graph of an equation
2.1/O3.statement: Every point on the graph is a solution of the equation, and no point off it is.

2.1/O3.name: Drawing a line
2.1/O3.statement: Choose three values of $x$, compute $y$ for each, plot the points, draw the line through them.
2.1/O3.note: $x=0$ and $y=0$ are the quickest choices; a line through the origin needs one more.

2.1/O4.name: Intercepts on a graph
2.1/O4.statement: An $x$-intercept is where the graph crosses the $x$-axis, where $y=0$; a $y$-intercept is where it crosses the $y$-axis, where $x=0$.

2.1/O4.name: How many
2.1/O4.statement: A graph may cross the $x$-axis twice, once, or not at all.

2.1/O4.name: Reading a value
2.1/O4.statement: Go up from the $x$-axis to the curve, then across to the $y$-axis; the profit at $x$ is the gap between the revenue and cost lines there.

2.1/O5.name: From the equation
2.1/O5.statement: For the $x$-intercept set $y=0$ and solve for $x$; for the $y$-intercept set $x=0$ and solve for $y$.

2.2/O1.name: Slope
2.2/O1.statement: $m=\dfrac{y_{2}-y_{1}}{x_{2}-x_{1}}$, the rise over the run between two points.
2.2/O1.note: Subtract in the same order on top and bottom; both differences can involve a negative.

2.2/O1.name: Horizontal and vertical
2.2/O1.statement: A horizontal line has slope $0$; a vertical line has undefined slope, since its run is $0$.

2.2/O2.name: Slope-intercept form
2.2/O2.statement: $y=mx+b$: $m$ is the slope and $b$ is the $y$-intercept, the value of $y$ at $x=0$.

2.2/O3.name: Reading m and b
2.2/O3.statement: Solve the equation for $y$ first; the coefficient of $x$ is $m$ and the constant is $b$.

2.2/O4.name: Graphing by intercepts
2.2/O4.statement: Find both intercepts, plot them, draw the line through them.
2.2/O4.note: $\frac{10}{3}$ is $3\frac13$: a third of the way from $3$ to $4$.

2.2/O5.name: Perpendicular
2.2/O5.statement: Slopes whose product is $-1$: each is the negative reciprocal of the other.

2.2/O5.name: Neither
2.2/O5.statement: Slopes that are unequal and whose product is not $-1$; the lines meet once.

2.2/O6.name: Point-slope form
2.2/O6.statement: $y-y_{1}=m(x-x_{1})$ for the line of slope $m$ through $(x_{1},y_{1})$; then solve for $y$.

2.2/O6.name: Two points
2.2/O6.statement: Find $m$ from the two points first, then use either point in point-slope form.

2.2/O6.name: Horizontal and vertical lines
2.2/O6.statement: Through $(x_{1},y_{1})$: the horizontal line is $y=y_{1}$, the vertical line is $x=x_{1}$.

2.2/O6.name: Year index
2.2/O6.statement: $x=\text{year}-\text{base year}$; a year given means substitute for $x$, a value given means set $y$ equal to it and solve for $x$.
2.2/O6.note: For the first full year, round $x$ up to the next whole number.

2.3/O2.name: A line from two data points
2.3/O2.statement: The two points give $m$; either point then goes into $y-y_{1}=m(x-x_{1})$, which is solved for $y$; predict by substituting the year's $x$.

2.3/O2.name: Rounding
2.3/O2.statement: Round $m$ to two decimal places first, then use the rounded $m$ in point-slope form.

3.1/O1.name: Function notation
3.1/O1.statement: $f(x)$ is the value the rule $f$ gives at $x$; $f(3)$ is $f$ at $3$, not $f$ times $3$.

3.1/O1.name: Algebraic input
3.1/O1.statement: Replace every $x$ in the rule by the input, in parentheses, then simplify.

3.1/O2.name: Numerical input
3.1/O2.statement: Substitute the number for every $x$, in parentheses, then follow the order of operations.

3.1/O2.name: Constant function
3.1/O2.statement: A rule with no $x$ in it, such as $f(x)=6$, gives the same value at every input.

3.1/O3.name: Domain
3.1/O3.statement: The set of inputs at which the rule gives a value, written in interval notation.

3.1/O3.name: Even root
3.1/O3.statement: Set the expression under the root $\ge 0$ and solve.

3.1/O3.name: Denominator
3.1/O3.statement: Set the denominator $\ne 0$ and remove that value.

3.1/O4.name: Cost, revenue, profit
3.1/O4.statement: Cost is fixed cost plus cost per item times items; revenue is price times items; profit is revenue minus cost.
3.1/O4.note: Cents go in as dollars: $30$ cents is $0.3x$.

3.1/O4.name: A model in function notation
3.1/O4.statement: A year is entered as $t=\text{year}-2000$; the output carries the units named in the sentence.

4.1/O1.name: Where the variable sits
4.1/O1.statement: Linear: $x$ to the first power, $y=mx+b$. Quadratic: an $x^{2}$ term. Exponential: $x$ in the exponent, $y=a^{x}$ or $y=c\cdot a^{x}$.

4.1/O2.name: Growth and decay
4.1/O2.statement: $a^{x}$ grows when $a>1$ and decays when $0<a<1$; $a^{-x}$ is $\left(\frac1a\right)^{x}$.

4.1/O2.name: Two points always known
4.1/O2.statement: $a^{0}=1$ and $a^{1}=a$; the graph passes through $(0,1)$ and $(1,a)$.

4.1/O3.name: Shape of $y=a^{x}$
4.1/O3.statement: Entirely above the $x$-axis, through $(0,1)$; approaches the $x$-axis on one side without touching it.

4.1/O3.name: Finding the base
4.1/O3.statement: From a point $(x,y)$ on $y=a^{x}$, $a$ is the number whose $x$-th power is $y$.

4.1/O3.name: Shifts
4.1/O3.statement: $a^{x+c}$ is $a^{x}$ shifted left by $c$; $a^{x-c}$ is shifted right by $c$.

4.1/O4.name: Evaluate or solve
4.1/O4.statement: A year given: substitute for $x$ and evaluate. A value given: find where the graph meets the horizontal line at that value, and read $x$.

4.1/O4.name: Money losing value
4.1/O4.statement: The future cost is today's price divided by the value of a dollar then.

4.2/O1.name: Exponential model
4.2/O1.statement: $g(t)=c\cdot a^{t}$ with $t$ the year index; evaluate at the year's $t$ and round as instructed.

4.2/O2.name: Logistic function
4.2/O2.statement: $g(t)=\dfrac{M}{1+ke^{-rt}}$; as $t$ grows, $e^{-rt}$ approaches $0$ and $g(t)$ approaches the ceiling $M$.

4.2/O2.name: On a calculator
4.2/O2.statement: Compute the exponent first, then $e$ to it, then the denominator, then the division.

4.3/O1.name: The equivalence
4.3/O1.statement: $\log_{b}y=x$ means $b^{x}=y$: the base stays the base, the logarithm is the exponent.

4.3/O1.name: Two named bases
4.3/O1.statement: $\log$ with no base written is base $10$; $\ln$ is base $e$.

4.4/O1.name: One logarithm equals a number
4.4/O1.statement: Rewrite in exponential form and solve.

4.4/O1.name: Logarithm equals logarithm
4.4/O1.statement: Combine each side into a single logarithm, then set the arguments equal.

4.4/O1.name: Check
4.4/O1.statement: Every solution must make each argument positive; a value that does not is rejected, and there may be no solution.

4.4/O2.name: Same base
4.4/O2.statement: Write both sides as powers of one base, then set the exponents equal.

4.4/O2.name: With logarithms
4.4/O2.statement: Isolate the power, take $\ln$ of both sides, and bring the exponent down: $e^{5x}=3$ gives $5x=\ln 3$.

4.4/O3.name: First full year
4.4/O3.statement: Solve for $x$, round up to the next whole number, convert back to a year.
